intent_record.intent_summary: Fixes kernel panic on PREEMPT_RT by replacing BUG_ON with graceful handling of concurrent pcpu_rt installation race condition
intent_record.what: Replaced BUG_ON(prev) with conditional handling that checks if prev is non-NULL, adds a WARN_ON_ONCE for PREEMPT_RT detection, performs cleanup of local allocation (dst_dev_put and dst_release), and returns the existing prev value instead of panicking
intent_record.how: Prevents kernel panic when another task on the same CPU has already installed a pcpu_rt during PREEMPT_RT preemption windows. Instead of crashing, the code gracefully cleans up its own allocation and reuses the existing route pointer

vuln_statements.explanation: The First Evidence Set explicitly shows '(none)' for pre-fix code lines from hunks, making it impossible to extract exact vulnerable statement text as required by the rules. The Second Evidence Set only provides function definition context (rt6_make_pcpu_route) around lines 1458-1465, which does not contain the actual vulnerable logic. Based on the root cause description, the vulnerability involves a race condition where task preemption occurs between verifying a NULL per-CPU route pointer and performing an atomic compare-and-swap operation to install a new route on PREEMPT_RT kernels. The actual vulnerable statement would typically involve a check of pcpu_rt being NULL followed by an atomic cmpxchg operation without proper serialization.
